name: Whatever They Call It
tagline: You let almost everything go. Just not the part that matters.
epigraph: Built for a tequila that had to find a name twice. Stone still crushes its agave.
glassware: tall highball glass (about 300 ml), three ice cubes
language_row: Wren's checks on v3: title block, whoYouAre and yours swap-tested against the family (in her turns); lint 0 errors, 3 warnings (gendered pronouns in yours 2–4, all Guillermo Erickson Sauza, accepted by Wren in r4). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/fortaleza-guillermo-erickson-sauza.md`. Oxford Companion, primary: SAUZA (pdf 1742–1744), TAHONA (pdf 1971), DIFFUSER (pdf 647). *Distiller Magazine* (American Distilling Institute), 27 Feb 2025, Q&A with Guillermo Erickson Sauza (secondary; his answers and the narration carded apart). *Cocktail Codex* p. 29. *Flavor Matrix* pdf 306 (Tropical Fruit page: carvacrol shared by tequila and oregano).
names_note: **Split three ways, 1–1–1, in the round-4 vote: Robin's pick.** *Whatever They Call It* (Wren: "The guest doesn't care what a thing is called, only what it is. And the story lives it"), *Small and Real* (Tomás: "it recognises Wren's one true thing, the little they won't let go; it praises the person, not the drink"), *What Stayed* (Hester: "The guest lets everything go except what stays, and in the story the old place is what stayed"). Tomás and Hester each wrote "I could take *Whatever They Call It*"; Wren wrote she could take *What Stayed* and *Small and Real*. Also in the room: *Not the Name*, *Easy on the Rest*, *Worth the Keeping*. The pour carries *Whatever They Call It* (the reading's title block) until Robin picks.
open_items: Name: a three-way split (see Names considered). Robin's pick; the pour carries *Whatever They Call It* meanwhile.
Fortaleza Blanco's 40% label strength is unsourced; the balance sweep covers 38–46%.
Fortaleza can be hard to find: the recipe note allows any blanco tequila made with a tahona.
